courses.title: Responsibility in community
courses.description: Six sessions across Mussar, Chassidus, history, and public life.

sessions.title: Take responsibility
sessions.hebrew: במקום שאין אנשים השתדל להיות איש
sessions.translation: Where there are no people acting humanely, strive to be a person.
sessions.prompt: What situation does the teaching imagine?
choices: A need for responsibility when others fail to take it up.
A rule that one must always study alone.
sessions.explanation: Mussar begins by naming the situation and trait a source addresses.

sessions.title: Courage to learn
sessions.translation: The shy person does not learn.
sessions.prompt: What tension does this line clarify?
choices: Humility can coexist with courage to ask and learn.
sessions.explanation: A trait becomes clearer when a source shows what it is not.

sessions.title: Joy and action
sessions.prompt: How can inner posture relate to practice?
choices: It can deepen action without replacing its concrete form.
sessions.explanation: Chassidic reading can illuminate practice without displacing its form.

sessions.title: A community in exile
sessions.translation: Seek the welfare of the city.
choices: Who is addressed in what historical setting?
Which current policy is automatically settled?
sessions.explanation: Responsibility is read inside a community and setting.

sessions.title: Public life without flattening
sessions.prompt: What makes a public-life comparison responsible?
choices: Naming a shared question while preserving source differences.
sessions.explanation: Wider-world learning requires both connection and distinction.

sessions.title: Choose a bounded practice
sessions.prompt: What is a responsible final step?
choices: Choose one modest practice tied to the source and revisit it.
Issue a ruling for all situations.
sessions.explanation: A source-grounded practice is specific, modest, and returnable.

production.prompt: This charge anchored the course. Type its English meaning from memory, in a few words.
